gloss: to be shy; to be embarrassed

definitions.gloss: to be shy; to be embarrassed; to feel awkward
definitions.explanation: to feel self-conscious or bashful, typically when receiving praise or attention

examples.english: I was embarrassed when they praised me.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{照|て}れながら{返事|へんじ}をした。
そんなに{見|み}ないで、{照|て}れるから。
examples.english: Don't stare at me like that, it's embarrassing.

examples.japanese: {愛|あい}してるって{言|い}われて{照|て}れてしまった。
examples.english: I got embarrassed when they said 'I love you.'

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}られると{照|て}れる{性格|せいかく}だ。
examples.english: She's the type who gets shy when her photo is taken.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {褒|ほ}められて{照|て}れる (get embarrassed when praised)
- {照|て}れながら (shyly, bashfully)
- {照|て}れくさい (feel awkward/shy)

RELATED WORDS:
- {照|て}れ{隠|かく}し (hiding one's embarrassment)
- {照|て}れ{屋|や} (shy person)
- {恥|は}ずかしい (embarrassed, ashamed - broader meaning)

NUANCE:
{照|て}れる implies a cute, bashful kind of embarrassment, often in positive situations like receiving compliments or attention. It differs from {恥|は}ずかしい which can be used for more serious embarrassment or shame.
